items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Chubby’s out there. The worst band leader in the world

ctx.x: Not good. In fact, I’m glad, the last time I talked to him I felt good because a month and a half or two months ago when I talked to him, he’s got kidney failure. And he was not going to take the dialysis. He’s not going to do that. He says, “I lived a good life, I’m 82, I want to go out—” I said, “Chubby, you’re crazy.” “Well Terry—” Anyhow I called him about, oh just a few days before I came here, a few days ago, and he changed his mind. He’s going to do that now. Three days a week, and I’m glad for him.…
Yeah? Who else was in that group when you were playing with him?

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Chubby and I had — a completely differently than Jack and I did.

ctx.x: Um hum. If I put Terry Gibbs and Jack Sheldon and Chubby Jackson in a room together, I wonder what might occur?

Well first you’d have to call the insane asylum. You call the insane asylum and make a reservation at the insane asylum. Because I don’t know it would be a lot of laughs. Talk about — Chubby and I had — a completely differently than Jack and I did. I’ll tell you about Jack. You know Jack could get a little risqué on stage. But when he worked with me he knew that he could not do that. I’m selling music and I’ll be the straight man, and Jack is funny without having to be dirty. You know he’s funny. He’s got a great…

Yes. So we’ve been at this for about an hour, I’ve really enjoyed this. I want to wrap up with a couple of questions. I wonder if you could have done anything else in your life besides being a musician.

items.title: Chubby Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: He has performed and recorded with Charlie Barnet, Conte Candoli, Terry Gibbs, Gerry Mulligan and many others.

ctx.x: Bassist Greig “Chubby” Jackson is one of the most dynamic performers in jazz history. He was born in New York in 1918 and started playing bass professionally in 1935. He was the spark plug behind the driving rhythm section in the first great Woody Herman band and brought Ralph Burns and Neil Hefti to the attention of Woody, who said of Chubby, “What an immense influence he had on us. And what enthusiasm!” He has performed and recorded with Charlie Barnet, Conte Candoli, Terry Gibbs, Gerry Mulligan and many…
Chubby lives in San Diego with his wife Margo, and he remains a treasure of jazz lore.
